4.0.0.en: Moreover he made an altar of brass, twenty cubits the length thereof, and twenty cubits the breadth thereof, and ten cubits the height thereof. [1]

4.0.1.en: Whoever approaches the temple from the east finds the entrance to the court of the priests. At this entrance the people come with their sacrifices and their offerings that they bring to the Lord. On the right, on the south side, is the brass altar, where the fire is kept burning continually and the priests offer the sacrifices (Ex 27:1-8; 38:1-7).

4.0.2.en: The brass altar here is the counterpart of the Mosaic altar at Gibeon (2 Chr 1:6; Ex 38:30), but it is larger than it.

4.0.3.en: The things made of brass are the altar of burnt offerings [1], the molten sea and the lavers for holding water [2-6], the covering for the doors of the court of the priests [9], and some of the vessels of the altar and other things [10-18].

4.0.4.en: The brass altar is not mentioned in the Book of Kings. Burnt offerings were offered upon it, and it was much larger than the altar that Moses made in the tabernacle of witness, whose dimensions were five cubits square, whereas the altar in Solomon’s temple measured twenty cubits square. For the people of Israel had increased, and had become numerous and rich, and it was hoped that they would be more godly through the experience of fellowship with God over these generations.

4.0.5.en: It was expected that the offerings for the altar of God would be far more abundant than before; therefore it was made of great capacity so that all the offerings could be placed upon it. For God had enlarged their borders, and it was fitting that they should enlarge His altars. What we offer ought to be in proportion to what is given to us.

4.0.6.en: The height of the altar was ten cubits so that the people worshipping in the outer court might be able to see the sacrifices of the burnt offering, and their hearts might be moved by it, and they might offer repentance for their sins, saying: It is of God’s mercy that I was not consumed, and this sacrifice has been accepted as an atonement for my transgression. Perhaps by this they would be led to the knowledge of the great sacrifice that would be offered in the fullness of time, the sacrifice of Christ! And perhaps their hearts would soar in the heavenly places when they saw the smoke of the sacrifices ascending.

4.0.7.en: The Holy Bible does not mention how they went up and carried the sacrifices to the altar. Some believe that they went up as upon a hill, without using steps (ladders), because the Law forbids this (Ex 20:26). Others hold that without doubt there was a sloping ramp for going up to the altar.

4.0.8.en: In the homilies of Origen on the Book of Joshua he gives us a living picture of the service of the altar and the sacrifices in the Old Testament as a type of what was fulfilled by the sacrifice of the Lord Christ on the Cross.

4.0.9.en: v We must explain the death of Moses, for if we understand how Moses died, we shall realize how Christ reigns. When you see the ruin of Jerusalem and the altar without sacrifice or offering or priests or Levites, when you see all this, say that Moses the servant of the Lord is dead.

4.0.10.en: And when you see that there is no one who comes three times (in the year) to appear before the face of the Lord, or to offer offerings in the temple, or to slay the Passover lamb, and eat unleavened bread, or to offer the firstfruits or to consecrate the firstborn child, then you realize the death of Moses the servant of the Lord.

4.0.11.en: But when you see the Gentiles entering the faith, and churches being built, and the altar being sanctified with the precious blood of Jesus Christ instead of the blood of sacrifices, and you realize that the priests and Levites are no longer occupied with the blood of goats and bulls, but with the word of God by the grace of the Holy Spirit, then it can be said that the Lord Christ has taken the leadership in succession to Moses...

4.0.12.en: When you see Christ our Passover sacrificed, and you eat the unleavened bread of sincerity, and the good ground of the Church bears fruit, thirty, sixty and a hundredfold, I mean the widows, the virgins and the martyrs. And when you see the people of the children of Israel increasing, that is, those who were born not of blood, nor of the will of man, nor of the will of the flesh, but of God, and so became the sons of God, those who had been scattered and whom He gathered together into one in His person.

4.1.0.en: When you also see people keeping the Sabbath day, not by ceasing from work, but by putting away sin, when all these things come to pass, then you realize that Moses the servant of the Lord is dead, and that Christ the Son of God has all the leadership[2].”

4.2.s.en: 2. The molten sea (the basin or laver)

4.2.0.en: 2 Also he made a molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim, round in compass, and five cubits the height thereof; and a line of thirty cubits did compass it round about. 3 And under it was the similitude of oxen, which did compass it round about: ten in a cubit, compassing the sea round about. Two rows of oxen were cast, when it was cast. 4 It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east: and the sea was set above upon them, and all their hinder parts were inward. 5 And the thickness of it was an handbreadth, and the brim of it like the work of the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies; and it received and held three thousand baths. 6 He made also ten lavers, and put five on the right hand, and five on the left, to wash in them: such things as they offered for the burnt offering they washed in them; but the sea was for the priests to wash in.

4.2.1.en: Also he made a molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim, round in compass, and five cubits the height thereof; and a line of thirty cubits did compass it round about. [2]

4.2.2.en: To the left of the entrance, toward the south side of the court of the priests, is the molten sea, in place of the small laver that stood in the court of the tabernacle of the congregation (Ex 30:17-21; 38:8).

4.2.3.en: This basin stands on the backs of 12 statues of oxen; perhaps these oxen point to the twelve tribes of Israel (2 Kgs 16:17), and they are in groups, each made up of three statues of oxen, each facing a different direction.

4.2.4.en: The priests were bound to keep their hands and feet clean, or else they were exposed to death (Ex 30:20).

4.2.5.en: The water for drinking in the Holy Bible points to the Holy Spirit (Jn 7:37-39), while the water for washing points to the word of God (Ps 119:9; Jn 15:3; Eph 5:25-27).

4.2.6.en: As the priests work in the temple they need water for washing, and need the word of God to wash their hearts by the Holy Spirit, the Giver of purity, holiness and continual renewal. This is what the Lord declared by washing the disciples’ feet before they partook of His holy Body and precious Blood on Holy Thursday.

4.2.7.en: This sea was like the laver in the Church of the New Testament, or like the baptismal font in the ancient churches. It is fitting for our consciences to be washed by true repentance, that we may serve the living God (Heb 9:14), and it is fitting for us to cleanse our hands and our hearts (Jas 4:8), so that we may hear the words of the Lord Christ: [He that is washed needeth not save to wash his feet], and be renewed by his repentance each time he enters to serve (Jn 13:10).

4.2.8.en: Josephus, the Jewish historian, holds that it was called a sea because of its enormous size. Others hold that it bore this name because of its symbolic work, for Solomon’s sea is a symbol of the first waters in creation, over which the Spirit of God was moving.

4.2.9.en: The altar and the sea are both symbols of their counterparts in the heavenly temple, made not with human hands.

4.3.0.en: And under it was the similitude of oxen, which did compass it round about: ten in a cubit, compassing the sea round about. Two rows of oxen were cast, when it was cast [3]

4.4.0.en: It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east: and the sea was set above upon them, and all their hinder parts were inward. [4]

4.5.0.en: And the thickness of it (and its depth) was an handbreadth, and the brim of it like the work of the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies;

4.5.1.en: and it received and held three thousand baths. [5]

4.6.0.en: The sea, or basin, was spacious. The rabbinic commentators believe that the priests used to bathe in it, immersing themselves in it [6].

4.7.0.en: He made also ten lavers, and put five on the right hand, and five on the left, to wash in them:

4.7.1.en: such things as they offered for the burnt offering they washed in them; but the sea was for the priests to wash in. [6]

4.7.2.en: There are ten bases of brass adorned with lions and oxen and cherubim, and upon each base a laver holding 230 gallons of water. These bases with their lavers are in the court of the priests on the right, and they stand on wheels that can easily be moved; they are used for washing the sacrifices, and perhaps for cleaning the temple in general.

4.7.3.en: When the water became dirty, it was poured out in a suitable place, and the lavers were filled with clean water from the molten sea.

4.7.4.en: These bases bearing the lavers are exceedingly beautiful with their many ornaments, so that the priests, the Levites and the people may realize that God sees in holiness and purity a special beauty, and that there is no separation between holiness and beauty (Ex 28:2; Ps 29:2; 69:6, 9; 110:3).

4.7.5.en: As for the laver, in the tabernacle of the congregation there was one laver, because all the priests were of the tribe of Levi, and even kings were not permitted to practice the priestly work. But in the temple, which points to the Church of the New Testament, there were ten lavers, five on the right and five on the left, because the priests of the New Testament are not bound to a particular tribe or a particular nation, for in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek; rather, all the priests are hidden in the greatest heavenly High Priest, our Lord Jesus Christ.

4.7.6.en: Such things as they offered for the burnt offering they washed in them [6]; for as the priests had to wash, so the sacrifices are washed. And we must cast away, with all diligence, all evil thoughts.

4.8.s.en: 3. The golden candlesticks and the tables

4.8.0.en: 7 And he made ten candlesticks of gold according to their form, and set them in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left. 8 He made also ten tables, and placed them in the temple, five on the right side, and five on the left. And he made an hundred basons of gold.

4.8.1.en: And he made ten candlesticks of gold according to their form, and set them in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left. [7]

4.8.2.en: A spacious place to which the light of day does not reach needs these candlesticks.

4.8.3.en: Josephus exaggerated in saying that there were ten thousand lampstands in the temple.

4.8.4.en: It resembles the lampstand that was in the tabernacle of the congregation.

4.8.5.en: The word of God is a shining lamp that gives light in a dark world.

4.8.6.en: In the days of Moses there was one lampstand, namely the five books of Moses (the Torah). The addition of other lampstands here points to the addition of other holy books. Thus the light shines more brightly, and the lampstands, that is, the churches, multiply (Rev 1:20).

4.8.7.en: Moses established one lampstand, which is the Jewish church, but in the temple of the Gospel it was multiplied, not only because of the many believers from among the Jews, but the churches also multiplied from all the Gentiles and peoples.

4.9.0.en: He made also ten tables, and placed them in the temple, five on the right side, and five on the left.

4.9.1.en: And he made an hundred basons of gold. [8]

4.9.2.en: In (1 Kgs 7:48) it mentions one table of the shewbread, because the aim of that book is to affirm the establishment of the kingdom of Israel, which was preparing the way for the coming of the Messiah, the Savior; but (2 Chr 4:8) points to ten tables in the temple, five on the right and five on the left, as though the Church of the New Testament, as a symbol of heaven, opens its doors to the new Israel in which the Jews are dissolved among the Gentiles, so that Christ offers Himself as heavenly bread to the peoples coming from the east and coming from the west, that is, from the ends of the world to its ends, without favoring any particular nation.

4.9.3.en: Perhaps twelve loaves were placed on each table, for as the house of the Lord grew greater, the service also grew greater. For in my Father’s house there is bread enough for the whole family.

4.9.4.en: These tables had a hundred basons or dishes of gold, for the table of the Lord is well prepared.

4.10.s.en: 4. The doors of the court of the priests

4.10.0.en: 9 Furthermore he made the court of the priests, and the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid the doors of them with brass. 10 And he set the sea on the right side of the east end, over against the south.

4.10.1.en: Furthermore he made the court of the priests, and the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid the doors of them with brass. [9]

4.10.2.en: The doors of the court of the priests were covered with brass [9], so that they would not be affected by the weather to which they were exposed; and doors of brass are mentioned in (Ps 107:16).

4.11.0.en: And he set the sea on the right side of the east end, over against the south. [10]

4.12.0.en: 11 And Huram made the pots, and the shovels, and the basons. And Huram finished the work that he was to make for king Solomon for the house of God; 12 To wit, the two pillars, and the pommels, and the chapiters which were on the top of the two pillars, and the two wreaths to cover the two pommels of the chapiters which were on the top of the pillars; 13 And four hundred pomegranates on the two wreaths; two rows of pomegranates on each wreath, to cover the two pommels of the chapiters which were upon the pillars. 14 He made also bases, and lavers made he upon the bases; 15 One sea, and twelve oxen under it. 16 The pots also, and the shovels, and the fleshhooks, and all their instruments, did Huram my father make to king Solomon for the house of the LORD of bright brass. 17 In the plain of Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredathah. 18 Thus Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance: for the weight of the brass could not be found out. 19 And Solomon made all the vessels that were for the house of God, the golden altar also, and the tables whereon the shewbread was set; 20 Moreover the candlesticks with their lamps, that they should burn after the manner before the oracle, of pure gold; 21 And the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs, made he of gold, and that perfect gold; 22 And the snuffers, and the basons, and the spoons, and the censers, of pure gold: and the entrance of the house, the inner doors thereof for the most holy place, and the doors of the house of the temple, were of gold.

4.12.1.en: And Huram made the pots, and the shovels, and the basons. And Huram finished the work that he was to make for king Solomon for the house of God: [11]

4.13.0.en: To wit, the two pillars, and the pommels, and the chapiters which were on the top of the two pillars, and the two wreaths, to cover the two pommels of the chapiters which were on the top of the pillars [12]

4.13.1.en: Here we see a brief summary of the things made of brass.

4.13.2.en: The following is noticed here: 1. Huram was a skilled, careful and conscientious craftsman, for he accomplished everything that was asked of him [11]. The king of Tyre called him “Huram my father,” and Solomon also called him so, because he excelled in his work, and he was counted a father of all the skilled craftsmen. 2. Solomon was very generous, for he made very many vessels [18] of every kind, so that the work in the temple might be completed quickly, and so that there might be vessels to be used whenever vessels were damaged.

4.13.3.en: The contributions came generously, and he also gave generously. And when he had made enough vessels for that time, he could not use the brass that remained for his own purposes, because it was dedicated to God and must be used for His service alone.

4.14.0.en: And four hundred pomegranates on the two wreaths; (two rows of pomegranates on each wreath, to cover the two pommels of the chapiters which were upon the pillars). [13]

4.15.0.en: He made also bases, and lavers made he upon the bases [14]

4.16.0.en: One sea, and twelve oxen under it [15]

4.17.0.en: The pots also, and the shovels, and the fleshhooks, and all their instruments, did Huram my father make to king Solomon for the house of the LORD of bright brass. [16]

4.18.0.en: In the plain of Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredathah. [17]

4.19.0.en: Thus Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance: for the weight of the brass could not be found out. [18]

4.20.0.en: And Solomon made all the vessels that were for the house of God, the golden altar also, and the tables whereon the shewbread was set [19]

4.20.1.en: The golden altar: it stands before the veil that separates the Holy of Holies from the Holy Place. Upon it the priests offer incense in the morning and evening, and they tend the golden lampstand (Ex 30:1-10; 37:25-29).

4.20.2.en: The offering up of incense points to the lifting up of prayers to God (Ps 141:1-2; Rev 5:8; Lk 1:8-10).

4.20.3.en: God gave Moses the special blend for the incense offered in the tabernacle of the congregation and the temple (Ex 30:34-38); no one may use this blend for any other purpose.

4.20.4.en: On the Day of Atonement the high priest uses the blood to cleanse and purify the golden altar (Ex 30:10). We cannot draw near to God without the atoning blood of the Lord Christ; for we may draw near only with clean hands and a pure heart (Ps 24:3-5).

4.20.5.en: Incense was burned upon it; perhaps it was made large, as was done with the brass altar.

4.20.6.en: Only here does the Holy Bible refer to a multitude of tables of the shewbread.

4.21.0.en: Moreover the candlesticks with their lamps, that they should burn after the manner before the oracle, of pure gold [20]

4.22.0.en: And the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs, made he of gold,

4.23.0.en: And the snuffers, and the basons, and the spoons, and the censers, of pure gold:

4.23.1.en: and the entrance of the house, the inner doors thereof for the most holy place, and the doors of the house of the temple, were of gold. [22]

4.23.2.en: How great is the work of Your hands within me!

4.23.3.en: v Who can build Your temple but You?

4.23.4.en: Who lays its foundation but Your grace?

4.23.5.en: Establish within me the pillars of silver virtue.

4.23.6.en: Your word is the pillars upon which the building of my soul stands.

4.23.7.en: Would that I were adorned with You, O Word of God, the All-beautiful!

4.23.8.en: v Enlarge the borders of Your temple within me, that it may be the place of Your delight and good pleasure.

4.23.9.en: May it expand with love for You and for all my brethren.

4.23.10.en: Then hatred, envy or pride will have no place in my thoughts.

4.23.11.en: And no wounding word will come out of my mouth.

4.23.12.en: v Set up a golden lampstand within me.

4.23.13.en: May it shine with the light of Your righteousness, and so every darkness within me be scattered.

4.23.14.en: By Your light the prince of the kingdom of darkness cannot creep into me.

4.23.15.en: v Set up the table of the satisfying shewbread.

4.23.16.en: Then I shall not feed on the love of the world and its pleasures.

4.23.17.en: Rather I shall enjoy the bread of angels, and my soul will be satisfied.

4.23.18.en: I shall feed on Your life-giving Body and Your precious Blood.

4.23.19.en: So I shall enjoy eternal life.

4.23.20.en: v Let fragrant incense ascend as to heaven.

4.23.21.en: May my prayers be acceptable before You.

4.23.22.en: May they carry Your sweet fragrance, and enter into Your divine throne.

4.23.23.en: v Accept my life as a sacrifice of love, a whole burnt offering before You.

4.23.24.en: I have nothing of my own to offer You.

4.23.25.en: Grant me to offer You of what You give me.

4.23.26.en: Sanctify my emotions, my feelings and my words, that I may offer love as a sacrifice well pleasing before You.

4.23.27.en: v Let all my energies, my gifts and my talents be holy vessels for You, never ceasing from service, worship and praise of You.
